title: Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story

pages.lesson:
LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING – SHORT STORY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How can we differentiate a short story from a novel?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the features of a short story for information
2. write a short story featuring a hero or heroine for creative expression

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Writing 8.3.1 Creative writing – short story makes your writing clear so others can read it easily.

• Look at the model your teacher shows. Notice shape, order, and spacing.

• Practise slowly first, then build neat speed.

• Check your work: Did you spell carefully? Did you use correct marks?

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Copy three model sentences neatly, leaving finger spaces between words.

Example 2: Spell five lesson words aloud, then write them without looking.

Example 3: Fix this sentence by adding capital letters and a full stop: “amina went to kisumu”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Write five neat sentences about your school using words from this topic.
2. Exchange books with a friend and check spelling or punctuation together.
3. Rewrite one messy sentence so it is clear and correct.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Complete a short guided paragraph in your exercise book.
2. List eight words from this topic and practise spelling them with a parent.
3. Write a short note to a friend using correct punctuation.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Read a short story from print or digital sources on community legends,
2. Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner interacts with digital content when reading a short story from digital sources on community legends.
3. Self-efficacy: It is promoted as the learner shows concerted attention by using the outline to write a short story on the hero or heroine. Values:
4. Patriotism: The learner identifies a community or national hero and heroine and their unique qualities.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we differentiate a short story from a novel?
2. Why is it important for a community to honour its heroes and heroines?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Neat writing helps the reader.
2. Check spelling and punctuation before you finish.
3. Practice a little every day.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
